title: Ways to Make a Fair Array
summary: Given an integer array nums, you need to determine how many indices you can remove an element from such that the resulting array is fair.
statement: Given an integer array nums, you need to determine how many indices you can remove an element from such that the resulting array is fair. An array is considered fair if, after the removal, the sum of the elements at odd indices equals the sum of the elements at even indices.
constraints: After removing one index, later indices shift parity; count removals yielding equal even-index and odd-index sums.
reference_solution:
def fair_array_removal_count(nums):
 total_even=sum(nums[::2]);total_odd=sum(nums[1::2]);left_even=left_odd=answer=0
 for index,value in enumerate(nums):
  if index%2==0:total_even-=value
  else:total_odd-=value
  if left_even+total_odd==left_odd+total_even:answer+=1
  if index%2==0:left_even+=value
  else:left_odd+=value
 return answer

hints: Removing an index swaps the parity of every later element.
Maintain left parity sums and remaining right parity sums around the candidate.
Remove the candidate from its suffix total; compare left-even+right-odd with left-odd+right-even; then add it to the left.
The comparison applies the exact parity shift while each running sum represents a disjoint side of the removed index.
